item.title: Subsea Telecom Cables Double as Abyssal Earthquake and Tsunami Arrays
item.description:
WOODS HOLE — Geophysicists working with transoceanic cable operators have begun reading tiny polarization shifts along active subsea telecom trunks to pinpoint undersea fault slips minutes before seismic waves reach coastal tide gauges.

Rather than lowering costly battery-powered ocean-bottom seismometers across abyssal plains, researchers inject coherent reference light into spare optical channels inside commercial repeater housings.

Turning Infrastructure Into an Observatory

Tiny acoustic strains on the seabed stretch the glass core by fractions of a nanometer, turning existing intercontinental data highways into continuous thousand-kilometer listening arrays.
